lead: Wristwatches, pocket watches, clocks, timers and their straps and parts, organised by type, then model family, reference and detail; brands live in the brand register.

depts.note: Organised by type (kind → model family → reference → detail); the brand view comes from the brand register. Smartwatches and GPS sports watches live in Phones, Tablets & Personal Devices (D2).

depts.t: Watches worn on the wrist and collected as model families; a smartwatch or GPS sports watch → Phones, Tablets & Personal Devices (D2), a watch carried in a pocket → Pocket watches.
depts.ax: What sets the watch apart: a job it is built for, a style, an electronic movement or a mechanism it shows?

depts.note: Period matters: verge and cylinder watches to about 1820, English and Swiss lever watches through the 19th century, American factory and railroad watches 1857–1969. Case style (open-face, hunter, demi-hunter) is a detail, not a kind.

b.v: railroad grade (17+ jewels, 5 positions, lever set) > adjusted > unadjusted; jewel count and adjustments are engraved on the plate
b.w: The railroad standards of 1893 onward are the collectors' grading ladder.

b.v: original case, dial and movement together > married or recased; redialled lowers value
b.w: Many Victorian-era revivals swapped movements.

b.v: solid gold > gold-filled > silver > base metal
b.w: Hallmarks and case-maker marks date and attribute the case.

b.v: unchipped enamel > hairlines > chips and restoration
b.w: Enamel dials are hard to restore invisibly.
Signed London, Geneva or American makers and early serial ranges command premiums.

s.t: Pocket watches defined by the age and escapement of the movement, such as the Nuremberg egg or the Waltham Model 1857; a graded railroad watch → Grade & complexity.

depts.t: Things that hold, store, maintain or replace parts of a watch or clock; smartwatch bands → Phones, Tablets & Personal Devices (D2).
depts.ax: What does it do for the watch: hold it on the person, store it, or replace a part?

ax: What is the object: a watch worn on the wrist, a pocket watch, a clock, a timer, or something that holds, stores or repairs them?
key: 1. Is it a strap, bracelet, chain, winder, box or replacement part for a watch or clock? → Straps, storage & parts
2. Is it worn on the wrist to tell the time? → Wristwatches
3. Is it carried in a pocket or on a chain? → Pocket watches
4. Does it time an interval, or tell the time from sun or sand (stopwatch, visual timer, hourglass, sundial)? → Timers & timing instruments
5. Is it a clock collected for age, maker, form or design (longcase, carriage, cuckoo, marine chronometer, flip clock)? → Collectible clocks
6. Is it a clock bought to use (alarm, wall, desk, travel)? → Everyday clocks
Precedence: a smartwatch is D2, a clock radio D3, a kitchen timer B5 and a chess clock E1; a strap or part is placed before the watch it fits.
